hero.headline: Chandigarh Online MBA in Family Business: Syllabus, Fees and Career Outcomes
hero.sub: UGC-DEB approved 2-year programme with Harvard and PwC certification options

sections.tldr: A specialisation aimed squarely at family enterprise, covering governance, succession planning, professionalisation, conflict resolution, family office management and managing diversification. Chandigarh University, NIRF Management rank 32, NAAC A+. Rs 1,65,000 after the 25% early-bird scholarship.

about.body:
Most Indian business is family business, and almost no management education addresses it directly. This specialisation does, which makes it unusual and, for the right person, unusually well aimed.

The subjects are Family Business Governance, Succession Planning, Professionalisation of Family Business, Family Conflict Resolution, Family Office Management, and Managing Growth and Diversification in Family Enterprises.

Conflict Resolution appearing as a dedicated subject is the tell that this was designed by people who know the territory. Family businesses rarely fail for commercial reasons alone. They fail when a commercial disagreement and a family disagreement become the same argument.

Succession Planning and Professionalisation cover the transition every family firm eventually faces: bringing in outside management, defining what the family decides and what it delegates, and doing it before a crisis forces the question.

This is the rare specialisation where the audience is obvious. If you are in line to run a family business, it is directly relevant. If you are not, it is narrow.

Two things are common to every Chandigarh specialisation and worth pricing separately from the subject list. AI for Managers appears in all of them, so the AI exposure is not unique to the technical tracks. And the programme runs in two tiers, where the higher tier bundles PwC co-taught modules and additional certification. Ask which tier your fee quote covers, because the subject list does not change between them.

Chandigarh University's NAAC A+ accreditation cycle carried a validity date of September 2026, so confirm the current grade at naac.gov.in before you rely on it.

Fees quoted here are indicative and change between intakes. Confirm the current figure, which tier it buys, the early-bird terms and what sits outside the tuition with the university in writing before you pay.

syllabus.note: Sem 1-2 shared core subjects across all Chandigarh MBA specialisations. See the main Chandigarh Online MBA page for core subject list.

subjects.name: Strategy, Business and Globalization
subjects.desc: Family business growth strategy, diversification decisions, globalisation of family enterprises, and conglomerate management.

subjects.name: Decision Science
subjects.desc: Financial analysis tools for family business valuation, capital structure decisions, and performance management.

subjects.name: Family Business Governance
subjects.desc: Family council structure, family constitution design, board composition, independent directors, and ownership protocols.

subjects.name: Succession Planning
subjects.desc: Succession process design, next-generation development programmes, transition from founder to professional management, and continuity planning.

subjects.name: Professionalisation of Family Business
subjects.desc: Separation of ownership and management, hiring professional CEOs, performance management systems, and family vs non-family employee management.

subjects.name: Family Conflict Resolution
subjects.desc: Family conflict typology, dispute resolution mechanisms, mediation in family businesses, and governance structures to prevent disputes.

subjects.name: Project Management
subjects.desc: Managing business expansion projects, greenfield diversification, and professionalisation initiatives as structured projects.

subjects.name: AI for Managers
subjects.desc: Digital transformation of family businesses, AI tools for operations, and technology adoption in traditional family enterprises.

subjects.name: Family Office Management
subjects.desc: Single family office structure, investment mandate, asset allocation for family wealth, tax planning, and philanthropy governance.

subjects.name: Managing Growth and Diversification in Family Enterprises
subjects.desc: Organic and inorganic growth strategy, family business M&A, new venture creation within family groups, and portfolio management.

subjects.name: Capstone Project II
subjects.desc: Applied family business project: governance charter design, succession plan, family office setup, or professionalisation roadmap.

whoHires.body:
Family Business MBA graduates from Chandigarh University Online pursue leadership in family enterprises and advisory roles:

**Career paths in family businesses:** Managing Director (family firm), CEO (professionalised family business), COO (family enterprise), Head of Strategy, Head of New Ventures

**Family office roles:** Family Office Manager, Head of Investments (family office), Chief Investment Officer, Philanthropy Manager

**Advisory and consulting roles:** Family Business Advisor, Succession Planning Consultant, Corporate Governance Advisor, Private Equity Analyst (family business-focused)

**External professional roles in family firms:** CEO (hired professional), CFO (family business), Independent Director, Business Advisor

**Key contexts:** Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Gujarat family trading and manufacturing businesses; North India real estate family enterprises; South India family business groups (chemicals, textiles, logistics); and family businesses across FMCG, retail, and services seeking professionalisation

**Where to verify placement claims:** ask Chandigarh University for its most recent placement report, in writing, covering your specific programme and mode. Online cohorts are often reported separately from on-campus ones, or not at all. EdifyEdu does not publish employer lists we cannot source, so treat the roles above as the job families this syllabus maps to, not as a record of who has hired from this cohort.

skills.body:
You should finish able to separate the family conversation from the business conversation, and to build structures that keep them separate.

Family Business Governance covers the instruments: family councils, constitutions, boards with outside directors, and the distinction between ownership rights and management authority.

Succession Planning covers the transition itself, from identifying and developing successors to the timing and tax structure of a handover, including the common failure of a founder who never actually leaves.

Professionalisation covers bringing in non-family executives: what to delegate, how to compensate people who will never own equity, and how to retain them.

Family Conflict Resolution covers mediation and decision rules set in advance. Family Office Management covers managing wealth separately from the operating business, and Managing Growth and Diversification covers the capital allocation question of whether to reinvest or spread risk.

comparisons.body:
Comparing Chandigarh Online MBA Family Business against peer programmes:

**vs ISB Family Business programmes:** ISB offers excellent executive education for family businesses. ISB's programmes are short-term executive programmes (not a 2-year MBA) and are priced significantly higher. CU's MBA in Family Business gives a 2-year NAAC A+ management degree credential with deep family business curriculum at Rs 1,65,000.

**vs SPJIMR Family Business Management programme:** SPJIMR's family business programme is on-campus. CU's online MBA is suited for second-generation business owners who cannot leave their businesses for 2 years but want the full MBA credential with family business specialisation.

**vs Chandigarh Online MBA Entrepreneurship:** Entrepreneurship covers venture-building. Family Business is the right specialisation for those inheriting or managing an existing family enterprise who need governance, succession, and professionalisation frameworks rather than startup creation tools. PwC's Family Business advisory practice (Tier 2) is specifically mapped to this specialisation.

fees.body:
The Chandigarh University Online MBA in Family Business offers 2 program tiers based on certification bundle:

**Tier 1 (Primary) - Standard with Harvard ManageMentor Certificate**:
- Actual program fee: Rs 2,20,000
- 25% Early Bird Scholarship: Rs 1,65,000 net payable (Rs 55,000 savings)
- Payment options:
  - Annual: Rs 82,500 per year x 2 years
  - Semester-wise: Rs 41,250 per semester x 4 semesters
  - Full upfront: Rs 1,65,000 one-time
- Included certification: Harvard Business Publishing certificate

**Tier 2 (Premium Upgrade) - 3-Certificate Bundle**:
- Actual program fee: Rs 2,20,000 (same base fee)
- 18% Early Bird Scholarship: Rs 1,80,400 net payable (Rs 39,600 savings)
- Payment options:
  - Annual: Rs 90,200 per year x 2 years
  - Semester-wise: Rs 45,100 per semester x 4 semesters
  - Full upfront: Rs 1,80,400 one-time
- Included certifications (3):
  1. PwC co-created and co-taught MBA modules (unmatched in India)
  2. CAPM (Certified Associate in Project Management) certification preparation
  3. Harvard Business Publishing certificate

**Additional charges (both tiers)**:
- Registration fee: Rs 1,000 (one-time, non-refundable)

**Zero-cost EMI**: Available directly through Chandigarh University (no external marketing partner or NBFC intermediary, a differentiator among Indian online MBAs). Contact our counsellor for current tenure options (6, 12, 18, or 24 months).

**Early Bird Scholarship terms**: Availability varies by admission cycle. The 25% Tier 1 scholarship and 18% Tier 2 scholarship are currently active but subject to timing. Reconfirm eligibility with our counsellor before enrolment.

EdifyEdu reconfirms fees with Chandigarh University each quarter. Please reconfirm current tier options, Early Bird eligibility, and fees with our counsellor before any payment. Fees listed are indicative.

For a full programme review and fee comparison, see our [CU Online MBA fees and honest review](/blog/chandigarh-university-online-mba-review).

certificate.body:
Graduates receive a Chandigarh University MBA degree certificate with Family Business noted on the marksheet, issued under UGC-DEB 2020 standards. NIRF Management rank 32 and NAAC A+ credentials add institutional credibility for family business leaders in banking relationships, government scheme applications, and investor interactions.

Tier 1 graduates receive the Harvard Business Publishing certificate. Tier 2 graduates additionally receive PwC Family Business and Private Business advisory co-teaching acknowledgement and CAPM certification preparation - the PwC Family Business practice advisory is a major differentiator for this specialisation specifically. DigiLocker verification is available.

faqs.question: What is the PwC partnership in Chandigarh Online MBA?
faqs.answer: Chandigarh University's premium tier includes full MBA modules co-created and co-taught by PwC industry experts. PwC's Family Business and Private Business advisory practice is one of the most active globally, advising hundreds of Indian family businesses on governance, succession, and growth. For the Family Business specialisation specifically, Tier 2's PwC co-teaching brings live advisory frameworks from real family business engagements. The PwC partnership is included in Tier 2 (premium) at Rs 1,80,400 net.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Tier 1 and Tier 2 fee options?
faqs.answer: Both tiers share the same Rs 2,20,000 base fee and identical curriculum. Tier 1 applies a 25% Early Bird Scholarship at Rs 1,65,000 net with the Harvard Business Publishing certificate. Tier 2 applies an 18% Early Bird Scholarship at Rs 1,80,400 net with three certifications: Harvard, CAPM preparation, and PwC co-taught modules. For Family Business, the PwC Family Business advisory co-teaching in Tier 2 is particularly valuable given PwC's deep family enterprise practice.

faqs.question: Is zero-cost EMI really available directly through Chandigarh University?
faqs.answer: Yes. Chandigarh University offers zero-cost EMI through the university's own payment infrastructure, not through an NBFC or external marketing partner. Tenures of 6, 12, 18, and 24 months are typically available. Confirm current options with our counsellor before enrolment.

faqs.question: Is this specialisation different from the Entrepreneurship MBA?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Entrepreneurship MBA is designed for founders building new ventures: startup strategy, venture fundraising, and innovation frameworks. Family Business is designed for those managing an existing family enterprise: governance structure, succession planning, professionalisation, and family conflict resolution. If you are inheriting or running a family business, Family Business is the right specialisation. If you are building from zero, Entrepreneurship is the better choice.

faqs.question: Does the programme cover family business succession in depth?
faqs.answer: Yes. Succession Planning in Sem 3 covers the full succession process: next-generation readiness assessment, transition from founder to professional management, continuity planning for unexpected events, and succession timeline management. Family Business Governance covers the ownership transfer protocol and estate planning interface. This is dedicated succession coverage designed specifically for family businesses, not a single topic within a broader management MBA.

chooseIf: You are a second or third-generation family business owner or promoter wanting a NIRF #19, NAAC A+ MBA with dedicated family business curriculum.
You want PwC Family Business advisory content (Tier 2) - PwC's private business practice is the most relevant advisory firm for this specialisation.
You need governance, succession, and professionalisation frameworks alongside a management credential.
You prefer zero-cost EMI directly through the university while managing your family business.
consider: You are building a new venture from zero rather than managing an existing family enterprise - consider the Entrepreneurship specialisation instead.
You need an ISB or SPJIMR family business programme for peer-networking with other family business leaders.
Your budget is under Rs 1.2 lakh and a lower-fee NAAC A++ alternative is necessary.
